memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But some of them could not celebrate the Passover on that day because they were ceremonially unclean on account of a dead body. So they came to Moses and Aaron that same day and said to Moses, "We have become unclean because of a dead body, but why should we be kept from presenting the Lord's offering with the other Israelites at the appointed time?" - Num 9:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a poignant scene. Some men were unable to keep the Passover at the right time because they were ceremonially unclean — they had been near a dead body, perhaps caring for a loved one who had died. Through no fault of their own, they were shut out of the great feast. And it grieved them.

Notice their response. They did not shrug and walk away, relieved to be excused. Instead, they came to Moses with an honest, longing question: "Why should we be kept from presenting the Lord's offering?" They did not want to miss out on drawing near to God. Their hearts ached to be included.

What a beautiful hunger this shows. These men treasured fellowship with God so much that being excluded troubled them deeply. They could have used their situation as an excuse; instead, they sought a way to still worship.

Have you ever felt left out of something spiritual — unable to attend, unworthy to come, kept back by circumstances or by your own failures? These men show us the right response: not to give up, but to bring our longing honestly to God.

The wonderful thing is what happens next in this chapter — God makes a way for them. He does not turn away a hungry heart. And in Christ, the way to God is now fully open; no one who comes to Him is turned away (John 6:37). If you long to draw near, that longing itself is precious to God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have you ever felt shut out of drawing near to God?
- Do you treasure fellowship with God enough to seek a way?
- What honest longing can you bring to God today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, give me a hungry heart like these men, longing to draw near to You. When I feel shut out, help me to bring my longing honestly to You. Amen.
